page: Microsoft Azure L48s_v3 is an LSv3-series server instance configured with 48 vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, the system features 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware allocation is dedicated, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It includes a substantial local storage capacity of 12,012 GB, which is Premium Storage capable, and lacks any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute and memory tasks, with specific areas of strength. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng benchmarks fall into the average category, as do the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. However, the instance demonstrates strong performance in Geekbench ray tracing and image processing tests. Passmark results show strong performance in CPU encryption and memory tests, while database operations and Redis SET operations, at 45.6 million operations per second, remain in the average tier. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 163.76 GB/sec for read operations and 70.56 GB/sec for write operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L48s_v3 offers high local storage density and a balanced 8.0 GB of RAM per core, making it a viable option for storage-heavy workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory-only instances. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on average-tier CPU compute performance, meaning it is less suited for pure high-performance computing tasks that require top-tier single-core speeds. It is best suited for large-scale databases, big data analytics, containerized applications, and moderate-scale LLM inference tasks, where its strong text generation speeds for small models can be leveraged alongside its massive local storage.
